text:
maya: Heads-up — I just saw a console page showing feature flags that belong to another org. Not a diffscreen, actual flags listed in the sidebar.
jon: Wait what, screenshot?
maya: uploading... (img) the sidebar shows `beta_ui=true` for an org that definitely shouldn't.
sasha: I grabbed logs from the edge proxy around the time. There's a lot of cache hits on the sidebar renderer.
oliver: Reproduced locally by mirroring session cookie routing. Looks like the sidebar is cached by session affinity key but missing org scoping.
kevin: Do we have code where cache key is built? That would explain it.
oliver: Yep. snippet from the render service: ```js
// renderCache.js
const cacheKey = `sidebar:${route}:${req.cookies.session_id}`; // <-- missing org_id
const cached = cache.get(cacheKey);
```
elaine: Oof. So if session_id is reused (sticky session moved) you could serve another org's sidebar.
jon: How does session affinity get assigned? proxy layer?
sasha: The LB sets a cookie `rwd_affinity`. Proxy uses that to pick downstream. If a user signs in and we reuse an existing affinity, and the render cache is keyed only on session, we get crossover.
maya: Important: the authenticated JWT still contains org_id. The renderer should assert JWT.org == payload.org before serving cached HTML.
kevin: Two separate problems: cache key missing org scoping, and lack of server-side assertion on cached payload. Both need fixes.
oliver: For immediate mitigation I can push a change to include org in cache key: `sidebar:${org}:${route}:${session}`.
jon: Long-term we need a policy: cache keys MUST include tenant identifier for any per-org UI surface, and renderers must validate token claims against cached content.
elaine: Also the proxy currently strips `x-org` header when routing to render service. Control plane adds it but it's lost in the sidecar. That needs to be preserved or replaced by signed claim.
sasha: Related telemetry idea: emit a metric when a cache hit occurs and token.org != cached.org. That would help detect any other exposures.
kevin: Does anyone object to the quick fix (add org to cache key + shallow assert)? If not I'll open PR.
maya: +1 — prioritize low-latency fix.
oliver: I'll do the PR for cache key. PR will also add a fast assert and a metric `cache_tenant_mismatch`.
jon: Debate: should we require org in path vs header? My vote: canonicalize tenant in auth token and server-side surface; avoid relying on headers that can be stripped.
kevin: Agreed. But header preservation at edge is cheaper short term. Long-term token claims.
elaine: For rollouts/UX: console should display a small badge when content is served from cache with TTL < 10s and say "stale" so support can spot oddities.
maya: Good idea. Also add an alert rule: `sum(cache_tenant_mismatch) > 0` -> paging for SRE in case of any cross-tenant exposures.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary deploy queued for render-service at 1830001145 (build #2321).
oliver: PR opened: github.com/redwoodinc/console/pull/456 (fix cache key + metric + basic assert). Canary in ~5m.
sasha: Postmortem template: short incident, root cause = missing tenant in cache key + header stripping at sidecar. Action items: 1) include tenant in cache key (oliver), 2) add server-side assert & metric (oliver), 3) ensure x-org preserved or substitute signed header (infra), 4) add console badge/telemetry (product/ux), 5) add alerting/pager (sre).
kevin: Also check other cached surfaces (saved searches, run lists, eval previews) — grep for `cacheKey` usages without `org` and open follow-up issues.
maya: I'll DM product to coordinate customer comms if needed.
jon: Thanks all. Keep updates here after canary.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary succeeded on 2/3 nodes at 1830001149. Monitoring for `cache_tenant_mismatch`.
elaine: Monitoring shows zero mismatches so far. Logging retention note: make sure these metrics are high-cardinality safe.
maya: Closing loop — rolling to prod after 30m stable canary. Thanks everyone.
